P01.title: Patch and lock down Ivanti Connect Secure on vpn-gw-01 to close the VPN-to-domain-controller path (P01)
P01.summary: The validation tool confirmed path P01. It broke into the corporate VPN appliance vpn-gw-01 (Ivanti Connect Secure) through CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 and got an authenticated shell. Admin credentials cached on vpn-gw-01 also worked on the IT jump host jump-it-01. From there, the jump host admin group's RDP rights let it open a session on the domain controller dc-01. Fixing vpn-gw-01 removes the entry point and breaks the whole path.
P01.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could take over the corporate VPN, reuse its admin credentials on the IT jump host, and log on to the domain controller. Control of the domain controller means control of every corporate account and system, which could support ransomware or a move toward operational networks. These two flaws are among the most widely exploited and have been used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Ivanti Connect Secure web and admin interfaces on vpn-gw-01 to known management networks. If that cannot be done, take vpn-gw-01 off the internet, in line with the KEV requirement to "discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable."
"Apply mitigations per vendor instructions" for CVE-2023-46805 and CVE-2024-21887 on vpn-gw-01, then upgrade it to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs.

Check vpn-gw-01 for signs of compromise, such as unexpected files, accounts, or configuration changes. If any are found, rebuild the appliance from a clean factory image before returning it to service.

Reset every admin credential cached on vpn-gw-01, starting with the admin account that also works on jump-it-01, and end all active sessions. Tell the Windows Server team so they can confirm the old credentials no longer work on jump-it-01.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-01 runs the vendor's fixed release and that its admin interface cannot be reached from the internet.
Confirm the old admin credentials taken from vpn-gw-01 are rejected on both vpn-gw-01 and jump-it-01.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P01.exec_line: Our corporate VPN can be hacked from the internet to reach the system controlling all company accounts; we are patching and locking it down now.
P01.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P02.title: Patch and restrict Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 to break the field office VPN path to dc-01 (P02)
P02.summary: Validated path P02 starts at vpn-gw-02, the internet-facing Fortinet FortiOS SSL-VPN for field offices, where CVE-2024-21762 gave an unauthenticated foothold. From there, the print spooler flaw CVE-2021-34527 on fs-02 (Windows file and print server) gave SYSTEM. On fs-02 a cached domain admin logon was present, and that credential reaches dc-01, the domain controller. Fixing the entry point on vpn-gw-02 breaks the whole path. The spooler flaw and the cached domain admin logon on fs-02 should still be handled as follow-up work by the Windows Server and Identity teams.
P02.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no password could move from the field office VPN to full control of the domain controller, which means control over every user account and Windows system in the corporate network. That would allow ransomware across the company, disruption of business systems that support grid operations, and a long, costly recovery. Both flaws on this path are widely used by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, limit the SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 (Fortinet FortiOS) to known field office addresses, or turn the SSL-VPN off until it is upgraded, in line with the KEV demand to discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
Upgrade FortiOS on vpn-gw-02 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-21762).
Check vpn-gw-02 for signs of compromise: unknown admin or VPN accounts, unexpected configuration changes, unfamiliar files, and unusual VPN sessions since the device was exposed.

End all active VPN sessions and reset the admin and local VPN account passwords on vpn-gw-02, then notify the Windows Server and Identity teams so they can patch fs-02 and remove the cached domain admin logon there.
verify_steps: Confirm vpn-gw-02 reports the vendor's fixed FortiOS release in its system status.
From an address outside the allowed field office ranges, confirm the SSL-VPN on vpn-gw-02 is not reachable while restrictions are in place.
Ask the security validation team to rerun the validation of path P02 and confirm it no longer succeeds at vpn-gw-02.
P02.exec_line: An internet-facing field office VPN could let attackers take over our main identity server, so Network Engineering will patch it and lock it down.
P02.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, the domain controller, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P03.title: Patch the Citrix NetScaler contractor gateway (nsg-01) to close the path to the email server (exch-01)
P03.summary: Validated path P03 starts at the internet-facing contractor gateway nsg-01 (Citrix NetScaler Gateway, owned by Network Engineering). CVE-2023-4966 on nsg-01 leaked session tokens, which allowed a contractor session to be taken over. From that session the email server exch-01 (Microsoft Exchange Server, owned by Messaging) responded to a server-side request forgery check for CVE-2022-41040. Fixing nsg-01 breaks the path at its entry point.
P03.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take over a contractor's remote access session and use it to reach the corporate email server. Control of email would expose sensitive utility communications and give a foothold for ransomware or further movement inside the corporate network. Both flaws on this path are widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, restrict access to the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to known contractor source addresses, or take it off the internet until it is patched.

Upgrade the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-4966); if no fix or mitigation can be applied, discontinue use of the gateway as the KEV entry requires.
After the upgrade, kill all active and persistent sessions on nsg-01, as the KEV required action demands, so stolen session tokens can no longer be used.
Check nsg-01 for signs of compromise, review recent contractor session activity for unexpected sources, and reset credentials for all contractor accounts that used the gateway.
verify_steps: Confirm the Citrix NetScaler Gateway on nsg-01 reports the vendor's fixed release and that internet access is limited to approved contractor sources.
Confirm that no sessions created before the session kill remain active on nsg-01 and that old contractor session tokens are rejected.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of attack path P03 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P03.exec_line: A flaw in our contractor remote access gateway could let outsiders reach the corporate email server; Network Engineering is patching and resetting sessions now.
P03.route_reason: The path ends at exch-01, the email server, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to Network Engineering, owner of nsg-01.

P04.title: Patch internet-facing plant edge firewall fw-edge-03 (PAN-OS GlobalProtect) to break path to the data historian
P04.summary: Validated path P04 starts at fw-edge-03, the plant edge firewall running Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS with GlobalProtect exposed to the internet. Command injection through the GlobalProtect portal (CVE-2024-3400) was confirmed on fw-edge-03. The firewall's management account password is the same as the local admin password on ot-jump-01, the IT to OT jump host, and hist-01, the plant data historian, accepts logons from that jump host. The validation agent stopped at the OT boundary and did not log on to ot-jump-01 or hist-01. Fixing fw-edge-03 removes the entry point for the whole path.
P04.why_it_matters: An outside attacker with no credentials could take full control of the plant edge firewall, then use the reused password to reach the IT to OT jump host and the plant data historian. That would put plant operating data and a foothold inside the OT boundary in the hands of an attacker, with risk to operational visibility and grid reliability. This flaw is heavily exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, on fw-edge-03 (Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS), enable the Threat Prevention IDs available from the vendor for this flaw and limit GlobalProtect portal exposure to only the networks that need it.
Upgrade PAN-OS on fw-edge-03 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-3400).
After the upgrade, check fw-edge-03 for signs of compromise, including unexpected files, configuration changes, admin accounts and outbound connections since the device was exposed.

Reset the fw-edge-03 management account password to a unique value not used anywhere else, and notify OT Engineering that the old value is also the local admin password on ot-jump-01 so they can rotate it.
verify_steps: Confirm fw-edge-03 reports the vendor's fixed PAN-OS release and that the Threat Prevention IDs remain enabled.
Confirm the fw-edge-03 management password no longer matches the ot-jump-01 local admin password, with OT Engineering checking from their side.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P04 to show it no longer succeeds.
P04.exec_line: An internet-facing plant firewall flaw could let attackers reach our plant data historian; patching the firewall and changing a reused password closes this.
P04.route_reason: The path ends at hist-01, the plant data historian, which is marked as a crown jewel.

P05.title: Patch SQL injection in Progress MOVEit Transfer on internet-facing vendor file exchange (mft-01)
P05.summary: Validated path P05: the internet-facing vendor file exchange mft-01 (Progress MOVEit Transfer) is vulnerable to CVE-2023-34362, an unauthenticated SQL injection. The validation tool confirmed the injection on mft-01 by reading only the version table. No other assets are on this path, so fixing mft-01 closes it.
P05.why_it_matters: An unauthenticated attacker on the internet could reach the MOVEit Transfer database on mft-01 and read, change or delete the files and records exchanged with our vendors. That could expose sensitive utility and partner data and disrupt vendor operations. This flaw has been widely exploited, including in ransomware data theft campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Progress MOVEit Transfer web interface on mft-01 so only known vendor IP addresses can reach it, or take it off the internet until it is patched.
Apply updates per vendor instructions: install the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs on MOVEit Transfer on mft-01.

After patching, check mft-01 for signs of compromise, including unfamiliar files in the web application folders, unknown or recently created user accounts, and unusual database activity or large downloads in the transfer logs.
Reset the credentials MOVEit Transfer on mft-01 uses for its database and service accounts, and reset any administrator accounts that look suspicious.
verify_steps: Confirm in the MOVEit Transfer admin console on mft-01 that the installed release is the vendor's fixed release.
Confirm from an outside network that the web interface on mft-01 is reachable only from approved vendor addresses.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P05 against mft-01 and confirm the SQL injection no longer succeeds.
P05.exec_line: Our internet-facing vendor file exchange has a widely exploited flaw exposing partner data; Enterprise Applications will restrict access and patch it now.
P05.route_reason: The path ends at mft-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Enterprise Applications owner team.

P06.title: Close internet-reachable admin setup flaw on Partner wiki (wiki-ext, Confluence Data Center)
P06.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the Partner wiki (wiki-ext), running Atlassian Confluence Data Center in the internet zone, exposes a setup endpoint that would let anyone on the internet create a Confluence administrator account (CVE-2023-22515). The agent stopped before creating an account. Fixing wiki-ext closes this one-step path.
P06.why_it_matters: Anyone on the internet could make themselves an administrator of the Partner wiki and read, change or delete everything shared there with partners. That could expose project, contract and operational details and let an attacker plant content or malware aimed at our partners. This flaw is widely exploited and has been used in ransomware campaigns.
fix_steps: Today, restrict internet access to the Partner wiki (wiki-ext) so only known partner and internal addresses can reach it, or take it offline if that is not possible quickly.

Apply the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-22515) to Atlassian Confluence Data Center on wiki-ext, or apply the vendor's mitigations; if neither is possible, discontinue use of the product as CISA requires.

Check wiki-ext for evidence of compromise per vendor instructions, including unexpected administrator accounts, new members of administrator groups, and unfamiliar plugins, and report any positive findings to CISA and the security team.
Remove any unauthorized accounts found and reset passwords for all legitimate Confluence administrator accounts on wiki-ext.
verify_steps: Confirm the Confluence version on wiki-ext matches the vendor's fixed release and that the setup endpoint is no longer reachable from the internet.
Review the Confluence administrator user list on wiki-ext and confirm every account is known and approved.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P06 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P06.exec_line: Our partner wiki could be taken over by anyone online; we are restricting access, patching it, and checking for signs of intrusion.
P06.route_reason: The path ends at wiki-ext, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes straight to the Collaboration Tools team.

P07.title: Close unauthenticated setup access on ConnectWise ScreenConnect (rmm-01) to cut path to virtualization cluster
P07.summary: Validated path P07: the internet-facing ConnectWise ScreenConnect remote support console (rmm-01) exposed its setup wizard without authentication (CVE-2024-1709), letting an attacker create an administrator account. From there, the support console can create a directory group that the VMware ESXi virtualization cluster (esxi-07) trusts for admin access (CVE-2024-37085), giving full control of the hypervisor hosts. Fixing rmm-01 breaks the path at its entry point.
P07.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take over the remote support console and use it to gain full control of the virtualization cluster that runs many corporate servers. That would let them shut down, encrypt or copy those virtual machines at once, disrupting business operations across the utility. Both weaknesses are widely used by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, remove internet access to the ConnectWise ScreenConnect management interface on rmm-01, allowing it only from approved internal or VPN addresses until patched.

Upgrade ConnectWise ScreenConnect on rmm-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-1709), applying mitigations per vendor instructions, or discontinue use of the product if mitigations are unavailable.
Check rmm-01 for compromise: review all ScreenConnect user accounts for unknown administrators, and review recent sessions, installed extensions and connected clients for anything unexpected.
Remove any unauthorized accounts, reset passwords for all legitimate ScreenConnect administrator accounts and any service credentials stored on rmm-01, and end all active sessions.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the ScreenConnect management interface on rmm-01 is not reachable from the internet.
Confirm that the setup wizard on rmm-01 can no longer be reached without authentication and that the ScreenConnect admin console reports the vendor's fixed release.
Request a rerun of the validation for attack path P07 to confirm it is closed.
P07.exec_line: Our internet-facing remote support tool could let outsiders take over our virtualization servers; we are locking it down and patching it now.
P07.route_reason: The path ends at esxi-07, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so the ticket goes directly to the IT Service Desk owner of rmm-01.

P08.title: Close internet-exposed Cisco IOS XE web UI on substation router rtr-sub-12 (path P08 to EMS data link)
P08.summary: Validated path P08 starts at rtr-sub-12, the Substation comms router running Cisco IOS XE, whose web UI is reachable from the internet and is on a version affected by CVE-2023-20198. From that router a route reaches ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, with no access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link. No traffic was sent to the EMS link during validation. Fixing the router breaks the path at its entry point.
P08.why_it_matters: An outside attacker could take full control of the substation router and use it to reach the energy management system data link, which carries the data grid operators rely on to monitor and control the system. Tampering with or blinding that link could disrupt grid operations and trigger reliability and regulatory consequences. This flaw is among the most widely exploited in the world.
fix_steps: Today, disable the Cisco IOS XE web UI (HTTP and HTTPS server) on rtr-sub-12, or limit it to trusted internal management addresses only, so it is no longer reachable from the internet or untrusted networks, in line with BOD 23-02.
Upgrade rtr-sub-12 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2023-20198).

Check rtr-sub-12 for compromise: look for unknown local accounts, especially any with privilege level 15, and for unexpected configuration changes, and immediately report any positive findings to CISA and the security team.
Remove any unauthorized accounts and reset all local and management credentials on rtr-sub-12.
verify_steps: From an external network, confirm the rtr-sub-12 web UI no longer responds on any internet-facing address.
Confirm rtr-sub-12 reports the vendor's fixed release and its local account list contains only approved accounts.
Request a rerun of the validation for path P08 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P08.exec_line: An internet-exposed substation router could let attackers reach our energy management system data link; we are locking it down and patching it now.
P08.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the Energy management system data link, which is marked crown_jewel. Grid Operations should also review the missing access list between the substation comms network and the EMS data link.

P09.title: Patch Apache Log4j2 in the internet-facing Outage map API (outage-api) to close remote code execution path P09
P09.summary: Validation confirmed that the Outage map API (outage-api), an internet-facing Java service using Apache Log4j2, is exploitable through CVE-2021-44228. A harmless test string sent in a request header caused outage-api to make an outbound DNS query. This shows the vulnerable lookup feature is active and reachable from the internet, and it is the entry point and only step on this path.
P09.why_it_matters: An attacker on the internet could run their own code on the outage map API server, then use it to tamper with public outage information or as a foothold to move deeper into the utility's network. False or missing outage data during a storm would mislead customers and crews and damage public trust. This flaw is among the most widely exploited ever and is used by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, block all outbound internet connections from the Outage map API (outage-api) except those it strictly needs. If that cannot be done quickly, take outage-api off the internet until it is patched.

Upgrade Apache Log4j2 in every component of outage-api, including bundled or nested libraries, to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2021-44228). KEV allows only two remediations: "Apply updates" or "remove affected assets" from the network.
Treat any temporary mitigation applied before the upgrade as acceptable only until the update is in place, then remove the reliance on it.
After patching, check outage-api for signs of compromise, including unexpected processes, new files, scheduled tasks, and unusual outbound connections since the service went live.
Rotate any credentials, API keys, and service account secrets stored on or used by outage-api.
verify_steps: Confirm that every Log4j2 library on outage-api, including those packaged inside application archives, is at the vendor's fixed release, and that no older copies remain.
Confirm that outage-api cannot reach arbitrary internet hosts, other than its approved destinations.
Ask the validation team to rerun the validation of path P09 against outage-api and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P09.exec_line: Our public outage map service has a widely exploited flaw letting internet attackers take control; the team is patching and restricting it now.
P09.route_reason: The path ends at outage-api, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it can go straight to the Customer Applications team.

P10.title: P10: Close unauthenticated takeover of Fortinet FortiManager firewall manager (fmgr-01) from the corporate network
P10.summary: The validation tool confirmed that the device registration port on fmgr-01 (Fortinet FortiManager, corporate zone) answers from the corporate user network and runs a version affected by CVE-2024-47575, a missing authentication flaw that lets a remote, unauthenticated attacker run code on the manager. This is a single-step path, so fixing fmgr-01 closes it.
P10.why_it_matters: The firewall manager holds and pushes the rule sets for the utility's firewalls, so an attacker who takes it over could rewrite rules, open routes toward sensitive or operational networks, and read the credentials it stores for managed devices. That would undermine the main barrier between business systems and the systems that run the grid. This flaw is already being exploited widely.
fix_steps: Today, restrict the device registration port on fmgr-01 (Fortinet FortiManager) so only the addresses of the managed firewalls can reach it, and block it from the corporate user network.
Upgrade fmgr-01 to the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2024-47575), as the KEV entry requires applying vendor mitigations or discontinuing use if none are available.

Check fmgr-01 for compromise: look for unknown or unexpected registered devices, unexplained configuration changes, and unfamiliar files or admin accounts, and escalate to incident response if anything is found.
Reset the FortiManager administrator credentials and the credentials fmgr-01 stores for managed firewalls.
verify_steps: From a host on the corporate user network, confirm the device registration port on fmgr-01 no longer responds.
Confirm in the FortiManager system information that fmgr-01 now runs the fixed release and that only expected firewalls are registered.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P10 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P10.exec_line: Our firewall management server can be taken over from the office network; Network Engineering will lock down access and patch it immediately.
P10.route_reason: The path ends at fmgr-01, which is not marked as a crown jewel, so it goes directly to Network Engineering.

P11.title: Patch Netlogon (Zerologon) on domain controller dc-01
P11.summary: Validated path P11 shows that the domain controller dc-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, Active Directory), owned by Identity, runs a version affected by CVE-2020-1472 (Zerologon) and accepts Netlogon secure channel connections from corporate workstations. The validation agent confirmed the vulnerable version only and made no change. The path is a single step, so dc-01 is both the entry point and the target, and it is marked crown jewel.
P11.why_it_matters: Anyone with a foothold on a corporate workstation could take full control of dc-01 and, through it, every account and domain-joined system in the corporate Active Directory. That would let an attacker push ransomware across the enterprise, impersonate staff and administrators, and potentially move toward systems that support grid operations. This flaw is widely exploited, including by ransomware groups.
fix_steps: Today, limit network access to Netlogon and RPC on dc-01 so that only domain-joined systems and administrative hosts that need it can reach it, and alert on Netlogon connections from unexpected workstations.
Apply updates per vendor instructions: install the vendor's fixed release for the affected CVE IDs (CVE-2020-1472) on dc-01 and on every other domain controller in the same domain.
After patching, turn on Netlogon secure RPC enforcement mode on dc-01 so vulnerable secure channel connections are refused, and allow-list only documented legacy devices that cannot comply.

Check dc-01 for signs of compromise: unexpected changes to the domain controller machine account password, new or changed privileged accounts, and unusual replication requests. If anything is found, treat it as an incident and reset the domain controller machine account and the krbtgt account.
verify_steps: Confirm on dc-01 that the vendor's fixed release for CVE-2020-1472 is installed and that Netlogon enforcement mode is enabled.
Review dc-01 system event logs to confirm vulnerable Netlogon connection attempts are being denied and that no unapproved devices are on the allow list.
Ask the security team to rerun the validation of path P11 against dc-01 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P11.exec_line: Our main corporate domain controller has a widely exploited flaw that could let an attacker take over all corporate accounts; patching is underway.
P11.route_reason: The path ends at dc-01, which is marked as a crown jewel asset, so the ticket needs human review before assignment.

P12.title: Restrict and add MFA to RDP on OT jump host ot-jump-01 to close corporate path to the EMS data link
P12.summary: Validated path P12 shows that any device on the corporate network, including a corporate desktop VLAN, can reach the RDP sign-in on the IT to OT jump host ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server, OT DMZ), which allows password-only sign-in with no multi-factor prompt. The energy management system data link ems-link-01 trusts logons coming from ot-jump-01, so anyone who signs in to the jump host can reach the EMS data link. The validation agent reached the sign-in prompt but did not attempt a logon. Fixing the RDP exposure on ot-jump-01 breaks the whole path.
P12.why_it_matters: Anyone who steals or guesses one corporate password could sign in to the jump host from an ordinary office desktop and then reach the energy management system data link. That link feeds the systems operators use to monitor and control the grid, so misuse could disrupt grid visibility or operations and trigger regulatory consequences for the utility.
fix_steps: Today, restrict inbound RDP on ot-jump-01 (Microsoft Windows Server) so it only accepts connections from a small, named set of approved administrator workstations or a dedicated admin subnet, and block it from all corporate desktop VLANs at the firewall.
Require multi-factor authentication for every RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01 and remove password-only sign-in.
Limit the accounts allowed to sign in to ot-jump-01 over RDP to a reviewed list of named OT Engineering users, removing shared and unused accounts.
Review sign-in logs on ot-jump-01 for unexpected RDP logons from corporate addresses, and reset passwords for any account with a sign-in you cannot account for.
verify_steps: From a corporate desktop VLAN, confirm the RDP sign-in on ot-jump-01 is no longer reachable.
From an approved administrator workstation, confirm an RDP sign-in to ot-jump-01 requires a multi-factor prompt and fails with a password alone.
Ask the security team to rerun validation of attack path P12 and confirm it no longer succeeds.
P12.exec_line: Any office computer can reach the gateway into our grid control systems with only a password; we are locking it down and adding MFA.
P12.route_reason: The path ends at ems-link-01, the energy management system data link, which is marked as a crown jewel, and the fix point ot-jump-01 is also a crown jewel OT asset, so changes need human review before assignment.
